predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the bishop's lands round Hildesheim: 'the official acknowledgement of Hildesheim as a Prince-bishopric' at the Mainz Reichstag on 15 August 1235 (the bishopric itself dates from 815)

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: 'In 1803, during the German Mediatisation, Hildesheim was secularised and its territory was annexed to Prussia'

ledger.x: 15 August 1235: Conrad II reaches 'the official acknowledgement of Hildesheim as a Prince-bishopric' at the Mainz Reichstag (infobox 'Imperial immediacy: 1235'); Louis the Pious had founded the bishopric in 815.
13 May 1523: the Quedlinburg Recess ends the feud, the 'last medieval feud'.
13 May 1523: the Great Stift is lost.
1803: 'during the German Mediatisation, Hildesheim was secularised and its territory was annexed to Prussia.'

wars.name: Hildesheim Diocesan Feud
wars.outcome: Hildesheim won at Soltau on 28 June 1519 but the Quedlinburg Recess of 13 May 1523 left it 4 of its 22 Ämter, the towns of Hildesheim and Peine and the Kleines Stift; the restitution of 1643 returned most of the rest.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary or area.
The Small Stift is drawn as two circles; the 1523 recess names Ämter, not lines.
Aerzen, Grohnde and Lutter stayed outside; the rest is the researcher's reading.
